'''''Malus hupehensis''''', [[common name]]s '''Chinese crab apple''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=MAHU2|taxon=Malus hupehensis|accessdate=27 January 2016}}</ref> '''Hupeh crab'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''tea crabapple''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the apple genus ''Malus'' of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Rosaceae.<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" /><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/8106071#page/219/mode/1up Rehder, Alfred. 1933. Journal of the Arnold Arboretum 14(3): 207]</ref>

It is [[native plant|native]] to China.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200010903 Flora of China, ''Malus hupehensis'' (Pampanini) Rehder, 1933.  <big>湖北海棠</big> hu bei hai tang ]</ref>

==Description==
''Malus hupehensis'' is a vigorous [[deciduous]] [[tree]] growing to {{convert|12|m|abbr=off}} tall and broad.{{cn|date=December 2023}}

It has pink buds, opening to fragrant white blossoms in spring. It produces bright red, cherry-sized crab-apples in the autumn.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-4053-3296-5|pages=1136}}</ref>

==Etymology==
''Malus'' is the ancient [[Latin]] name for apple trees.<ref name="gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp 205, 249</ref>

''Hupehensis'' means 'from [[Hubei]] province, [[China]]'. 'Hubei' was formerly spelled 'Hupeh' or 'Hupei' in [[English language|English]].<ref name="gledhill" />

==Uses==
The plant is cultivated as an [[ornamental tree]], for planting in gardens. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Malus hupehensis'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/10774/Malus-hupehensis/Details |access-date=3 January 2021}}</ref>
